newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy closer to EMU but problems ahead - Istat.
newsitem.headline: Italy closer to EMU but problems ahead - Istat.

text.p: Italy has made significant advances towards meeting the entry terms of the European single currency but is facing a problem with unemployment and has to tackle welfare reform, Italy's statistics office said on Wednesday.
"Italy has covered a large part of the road needed to comply with the terms of the Maastricht Treaty," Istat said in its annual report.

"Inflation is under control, the exchange rate is stabile, interest rates are approaching those of other countries and the difficulties, as far as the deficit/GDP ratio is concerned, don't seem very different from those in other major European states," it added.

However it said some worries remained about public finances, including Italy's ability to keep accounts under control over the medium-to-long term, and added that the country had to think about structural spending changes.
Looking at the welfare state, Istat said that while Italy actually spent less on social benefits than the European Union average, it spent proportionally more on pensions.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi opened talks with union leaders on Tuesday at the start of what are expected to be lengthy negotiations over proposed welfare reform.
Istat also noted that there was little state protection for the unemployed at a time when the jobless total was rising and the economy was struggling to grow.

"In more recent months a largely negative atmosphere has prevailed as far as the creation of new jobs is concerned," the report said. Latest Istat data put the unemployment rate at 12.4 percent in January from 12.2 percent in October.

"The growing prospects of European convergence makes intervention aimed at boosting the mid-term development of the economy more urgent -- a necessary condition to overcome social contradictions and tensions," Istat said. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
